([[Saly, Senegal]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 10 | draft_team = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = [[2022 BAL season|2022]] | team1 = [[Cobra Sport]] | years2 = [[2023 BAL season|2023]] | team2 = [[AS Douanes (basketball)|AS Douanes]] | years3 = [[2024 BAL season|2024]] | team3 = [[City Oilers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team4 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years5 = {{nbay|2025|start}} | team5 = →[[Valley Suns]] | highlights = * [[BAL rebounding leader]] ([[2024 BAL season|2024]]) * [[Basketball Without Borders]] MVP (2023) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team ([[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) }} '''Khaman Madit Maluach''' (born 14 September 2006) is a South Sudanese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Standing at {{height|ft=7|in=1}}, he plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He is also a current member of the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]], which he joined at the age of 16. ==Early life== Born in [[Rumbek]], [[Sudan]] (now [[South Sudan]]), Maluach grew up in [[Kawempe]], a small town in [[Uganda]], as a refugee with his siblings and mother. He attended Bethel Covenant College in Bwebajja.{{Cite news |last=Mutebi |first=Charles |date=23 March 2024 |title=Next big thing? The incredible rise of 'City Oilers' Khaman Maluach |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/sports/next-big-thing-the-incredible-rise-of-city-oi-NV_184225 |access-date=19 April 2024 |work=New Vision}}{{cite web |last=Grez |first=Matias |title=The unique visa hurdles NBA draft prospect Khaman Maluach will face when traveling for road trips |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/06/25/sport/nba-draft-khaman-maluach-spt |website=CNN |access-date=26 June 2025 |language=en |date=25 June 2025}} In 2019, Maluach was encouraged to play basketball by a [[boda boda]] motorcyclist who had stopped down when he saw the tall Maluach walking along the road. He attended a local camp organised by [[Luol Deng]] and started playing basketball.{{Citation |title=Khaman Maluach Interview {{!}} NBA Academy Games {{!}} 7.6.23 | date=10 July 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=efck_ZnO-74 |access-date=12 August 2023 |language=en|publisher=YouTube}} He later joined the [[NBA Academy Africa]] in [[Saly, Senegal]], where basketball is combined with education.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} ==College career== On 6 March 2024, Maluach announced his commitment to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. Ranked as the third-best prospect in the 2025 [[NBA draft]] by [[ESPN]] at the time, he chose Duke over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{Cite web |date=6 March 2024 |title=Khaman Maluach, top big man in 2024 class, commits to Duke |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39666849 |access-date=18 April 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|last=Givony|first=Johnathan}} He stated that this was due to the impression [[Zion Williamson]] had on him when he was younger.{{Cite web |date=29 September 2024 |title=Duke Prospect Explains Why he Picked the Blue Devils |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/duke-khaman-maluach-picked-blue-devils-zion-williamson |access-date=30 September 2024 |website=SI.com |language=en-US|last=Stiles|first=Rylan}} Maluach opted to play with number 9, honouring [[Luol Deng]].{{Cite web |last=Rankin |first=Duane |title=Khaman Maluach 'excited' to wear Phoenix Suns jersey, fulfills NBA dream |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2025/06/25/phoenix-suns-land-khaman-maluach-with-10th-pick-in-2025-nba-draft/84361451007/ |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US|date=25 June 2025}} He would be joined by two other top-rated prospects in [[Cooper Flagg]] and [[Kon Knueppel]] (both of whom would later end up being top-five selections in the [[2025 NBA draft]]) during the season he was with Duke. Maluach averaged 8.6 points on 71.2% shooting, as well as 6.6 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game at Duke. ==Professional career== ===Basketball Africa League (2022–2024)=== Maluach played for the South Sudanese professional team [[Cobra Sport]] in the [[2022 BAL season]], as part of the BAL Elevate program. Through this programme, one NBA Academy Africa player was assigned to each [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL) team on an amateur contract.{{Cite web |date=2 March 2022 |title=NBA launches BAL Elevate, placing Academy players with teams for tournament |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/33403664 |access-date=18 April 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He made his BAL debut on 9 April 2022 against defending champions [[Zamalek SC Basketball|Zamalek]], scoring two points and recording two rebounds in seven minutes.{{Cite web |title=Khaman Maluach, Basketball Player |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/252887/khaman-maluach |access-date=29 October 2022 |website=Proballers |language=en}} In March 2023, Maluach played in his second BAL season after he was drafted first among the academy prospects by the [[AS Douanes (basketball)|AS Douanes]], the defending Senegalese champions. The Douanes reached the [[2023 BAL Final|final]], in which Maluach started and contributed 2 points and 4 rebounds, as they lost to [[Al Ahly (basketball)|Al Ahly]]. He attended the 2023 [[Basketball Without Borders]] in [[Johannesburg]], South Africa, and was named the camp's MVP.{{Cite web |title=Egypt's Hassan, Malauch of South Sudan named MVPs of BWB Africa camp |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/egypt-s-hassan-malauch-of-south-sudan-named-mvps-of-bwb-africa-camp |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=10 August 2023 |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title=South Sudan's Khaman Maluach and Egypt's Aisha Hassan named BWB Africa Most Valuable Players |url=https://ojbsport.com/2023/08/02/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-and-egypts-aisha-hassan-named-bwb-africa-most-valuable-players/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230802005108/https://ojbsport.com/2023/08/02/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-and-egypts-aisha-hassan-named-bwb-africa-most-valuable-players/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=2 August 2023 |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=OJB Sport |language=en}} On 4 March 2024, it was announced that Maluach was drafted by the Ugandan club [[City Oilers]] for the [[2024 BAL season]].{{Cite web |date=4 March 2024 |title=Top NBA Draft prospects Ulrich Chomche and Khaman Maluach land on BAL teams for 2024 season |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/39651148 |access-date=18 April 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|last=Solms|first=Leonard}} On 19 April, Maluach had 16 points and 8 rebounds in his Oilers debut in a 76–99 loss to [[Al Ahly (basketball)|Al Ahly]].{{Cite web |title=Al Ahly vs. City Oilers |url=https://fibalivestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/u/BAL/2410682/ |access-date=19 April 2024 |website=FIBA Livestats}} One day later, on 20 April, Maluach set new career highs with 29 points and 11 rebounds in a 88–101 loss against [[Bangui Sporting Club|Bangui]].{{Cite web |date=21 April 2024 |title=How the first Maluach v Darlan duel of the season turned out |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/how-the-first-maluach-v-darlan-duel-of-the-season-turned-out |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en}} On 24 April, Maluach had 16 points, 19 rebounds and 7 blocks in a 68–79 loss to [[Al-Ahly Ly SC (basketball)|Al-Ahly Ly]].{{Cite web |title=LiveStats |url=https://geniussports.com/ |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=geniussports.com}} His 19 rebounds set a new career high, and his 7 blocks set a then-league record for most blocks [[List of BAL records|by any player in a BAL game]].{{Cite web |title=Opong says City Oilers can't throw the towel in after dropping to 0-3 |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/opong-says-city-oilers-cant-throw-the-towel-in-after-dropping-to-0-3 |access-date=23 April 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en|date=23 April 2024}} Despite the Oilers being eliminated, Maluach averaged 17.5 points, a league-leading 13.5 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks per game over his six performances.{{Cite web |title=Highlights from the 2024 Nile Conference |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/highlights-from-the-2024-nile-conference |access-date=2 May 2024 |website=The BAL |language=en}} ===Phoenix Suns (2025–present)=== On 25 June 2025, Maluach was drafted 10th overall by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]]; however, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as part of the [[Kevin Durant]] trade that was finalized on 6 July 2025.{{Cite web |date=26 June 2025 |title=Sources: Suns acquire Mark Williams, draft Khaman Maluach |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45586152 |access-date=18 April 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|last=McMenamin|first=Dave}} Alongside Maluach, the Suns acquired [[Jalen Green]], [[Dillon Brooks]], the draft rights to [[Rasheer Fleming]] and [[Koby Brea]], and a 2026 second-round pick, as part of a seven-team deal.{{cite news |title=PHOENIX SUNS ACQUIRE DILLON BROOKS, JALEN GREEN AND DRAFT RIGHTS TO KHAMAN MALUACH, RASHEER FLEMING AND KOBY BREA IN SEVEN-TEAM TRADE |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/phoenix-suns-acquire-dillon-brooks-jalen-green-and-draft-rights-to-khaman-maluach-rasheer-fleming-and-koby-brea-in-seven-team-trade |access-date=6 July 2025 |work=NBA.com |date=6 July 2025}} Maluach became the highest-drafted player ever from the [[NBA Academy Africa]], as well as from the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).{{Cite web |date=26 June 2025 |title=South Sudan's Maluach becomes highest drafted ex-NBA Academy Africa and BAL player |url=https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/tea/magazine/maluach-highest-drafted-ex-nba-academy-africa-and-bal-player-5096632 |access-date=27 June 2025 |website=The EastAfrican |language=en}} On 15 December 2025, Maluach was assigned to the Suns' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Valley Suns]].{{cite web |title=Suns' Khaman Maluach: Assigned to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-khaman-maluach-assigned-to-g-league-508718/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=18 December 2025 |date=16 December 2025}} On 8 April 2026, Maluach made his first NBA start, recording four points, 14 rebounds, and three blocks during a 112–107 victory over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=Suns' Khaman Maluach: Big defensive effort in first start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-khaman-maluach-big-defensive-effort-in-first-start/|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==National team career== In August 2023, Maluach was selected for the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan national team]] roster for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. At age 16, he was the youngest player on the Bright Stars' roster.{{Cite web |title=Lakers forward Wenyen Gabriel fortifies South Sudan World Cup squad |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/lakers-forward-wenyen-gabriel-fortifies-south-sudan-world-cup-squad |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=8 August 2023 |language=en}} On 28 August 2023, he made his debut in a victory against [[China men's national basketball team|China]], becoming the third-youngest player to appear in a World Cup game.{{Cite web |title=South Sudan's Khaman Maluach, 16, makes FIBA World Cup debut |url=https://abcnews.com/Sports/south-sudans-khaman-maluach-16-makes-fiba-world/story?id=102616871 |access-date=2026-04-18 |website=ABC News |language=en|date=2023-08-23|agency=ESPN.com news services}} Maluach and South Sudan were the best-ranked African team in the tournament, and thus qualified for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]], another milestone in the national team's history.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}} He played with South Sudan at the 2024 Olympics and was the youngest player in the tournament. He averaged 0.7 points in 4.3 minutes per game over three games, playing a minor role for the Bright Stars.{{Cite web |title=Khaman Maluach International Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/khaman-maluach-1.html |access-date=26 June 2025 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} ==Player profile== Maluach has a
